source_snapshot.title: UAE driving tests: Why scoring 75% may still not be enough to pass
source_snapshot.text: Learner drivers in the UAE could score at least 75 per cent in their practical driving test and still fail if they make a dangerous mistake, under new regulations that are set to take effect on January 1, 2027, a judicial official told Khaleej Times. The rules, published in the official gazette on October 21, require UAE residents applying for a driving licence to achieve a minimum score of 75 per cent in both theory and practical tests. However, meeting that threshold does not guarantee a pass, as certain dangerous errors can result in automatic failure regardless of the overall score. Judicial counsellor Hesham Elrafei explained that the regulations distinguish between serious mistakes that can trigger automatic failure and smaller errors that are dealt with through the marking system, where points can be deducted. However, the law does not establish one identical marking system for every driving school across the UAE. Detailed assessment criteria are determined by the relevant licensing authorities. When can a learner automatically fail? Under Article 68, dangerous mistakes can result in failure even when a candidate has achieved the required overall score. Examples include losing control of the car, hitting a kerb or barrier, ignoring traffic signs or signals, and making dangerous errors when changing gears. If an examiner has to speak to or physically intervene with a learner to prevent a dangerous situation, the candidate can automatically fail the test. The regulation does not, however, explicitly require the examination to end immediately following such an incident. It also does not specify how feedback must be provided to candidates who fail, leaving these procedures to the relevant licensing authorities. What happens if a learner fails? Under Article 69, applicants who fail the practical driving test will be given another test date by the relevant licensing authority. The regulation does not prescribe a fixed waiting period before a learner can retake the test, nor does it require additional driving lessons as a condition for taking it again. It also does not specify whether candidates must pay another test fee following failure. These details depend on the procedures of the relevant licensing authority. Will the rules affect learners already taking lessons? The new regulations do not exempt applicants who began driving lessons or booked their tests before that date. Learners taking their tests from January 1 should therefore expect to be assessed under the new requirements, even if they began their training months earlier. Driving schools and licensing authorities will need to update their testing procedures, although the regulation does not set out specific preparations they must complete ahead of implementation.

claims.claim: From January 1, 2027, new practical driving test rules will take effect in the UAE.
To pass the test, a minimum score of 75% is required.
Dangerous mistakes can lead to automatic failure even if the overall score is high.
Examples of dangerous mistakes include losing control of the car, hitting a kerb, ignoring traffic signs, and dangerous gear changes.
If the examiner intervenes to prevent an accident, the candidate can fail automatically.
The rules apply to all candidates taking tests from January 1, 2027, regardless of when they started training.

summary_ru: 🚗 Новые правила сдачи водительских экзаменов в ОАЭ с 2027 года 📅 С 1 января 2027 года в ОАЭ вступят в силу новые правила сдачи практического экзамена на водительские права. Для прохождения теста нужно набрать минимум 75% баллов, но опасные ошибки могут привести к автоматическому провалу, даже при высоком общем результате. К таким ошибкам относятся потеря контроля над автомобилем, столкновение с бордюром, игнорирование дорожных знаков и опасные действия при переключении передач. Если экзаменатор вмешивается для предотвращения аварии, кандидат также может не пройти тест. Правила распространяются на всех, кто сдаёт экзамены с 1 января 2027 года, независимо от даты начала обучения.
